Subject: SLA discussion: uptime & latency commitments

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our ops team asked me to get the SLA details in writing so we can run them by finance. A few asks from our side:

- Can Redwood confirm a standard committed uptime (we were thinking 99.95%) and the proposed monthly credit bands if you miss it?
- We also need a latency commitment for our inference traffic (target p95 <= 300 ms). If you can’t guarantee that across the fleet, what credit bands would apply to latency regressions?
- Finally, procurement asked for the monthly credit cap and any carveouts for maintenance or scaling events.

Happy to take a template and a short explanation of how credits are calculated (rolling windows, lookback, etc.). Looking to close on this before our procurement review next Thursday.

Best,

Ethan —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together a compact proposal (summary below) and attached a redlineable draft SLA + a one-page table you can drop into your purchase order. High level: we can commit to a provisioned uptime SLO of 99.95% by default, with a tiered monthly credit schedule and a separate latency banding construct. Key points: 

1) Provisioned uptime (primary SLO)
   - Committed: 99.95% monthly.
   - Remedy bands (monthly):
     * >= 99.95% — no credit
     * 99.90% - 99.95% — credit = 10% of monthly fee
     * 99.50% - 99.90% — credit = 30% of monthly fee
     * < 99.50% — credit = 50% of monthly fee
   - Credits applied against the invoice for the affected month.

2) Latency (secondary SLO, p95 measured at edge node)
   - Target: p95 <= 300 ms. Separate latency-credit pool applies when p95 exceeds target for the billing month.
   - Latency bands (monthly):
     * p95 <= 300 ms — no latency credit
     * 300-500 ms — credit = 5% of monthly fee (capped separately)
     * > 500 ms — credit = 15% of monthly fee
   - Latency credits do not stack with the primary uptime credit — we apply the larger of the two remedies for that month (we can also discuss additive models if you prefer).

3) Caps, windows, and carveouts
   - Monthly cap: credits will not exceed 20% of the monthly invoice for standard hosted accounts (we can expand for dedicated licenses).
   - Measurement window: rolling calendar month (UTC) with instrumentation tied to request routing logs & health traces.
   - Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (>=48 hrs notice for >2 hr windows), customer-induced misconfiguration, DDoS or force majeure, region-level cloud provider outages.

4) Operational terms
   - Root cause summary and remediation plan provided within 3 business days when remedy is triggered.
   - Option for a dedicated capacity addendum (Dedicated product) if you need stricter guarantees — that would change caps and remedies.

Attached: redline_sla_draft_v1.pdf (SLA text), provisioned_uptime_table.xlsx (credit math and examples).

If this looks broadly acceptable I’ll loop in Legal for a lightweight amendment and Ben/Aditya will help us validate the credit calculations for high-throughput patterns.

Cheers,
Laura

Looping in a quick technical tweak from the infra side — two suggestions before we send to Procurement:

- Measurement window: recommend we include a 30-day rolling lookback for operational remediation triggers but keep remedy calculations on a calendar-month invoice basis. That avoids edge cases where a transient 24hr degradation skews a single invoice unfairly.

- Latency banding: suggest a micro-band at p95 300-350 ms with a nominal 2% credit (instead of jumping straight to 5%). For heavy-batched inference customers that run close to the p95 target, this gives a softer ramp into material credits.

I redlined the attached PDF with these proposals (file: redline_sla_draft_v1.pdf). If Laura agrees I’ll finalize the math in provisioned_uptime_table.xlsx and we can produce a one-pager for Stratify procurement.

—Ben
